biography.plain_text: David Russell is an Australian infrastructure investor and co-founder of Equis. Trained in law and economics, he worked as a lawyer and Macquarie executive before establishing the investment firm. Its renewable-energy portfolio was sold to Global Infrastructure Partners and its partners, generating substantial proceeds for Equis founders. He is based in Melbourne.

long_biography.plain_text:
Leaving Macquarie cost Equis founder David Russell relationships he had expected to retain. Contacts who had welcomed a senior banker were less receptive to a new business without the institution behind it. His team consequently built its investor base afresh, without bringing across major investors from his former employer.

Russell gave local project teams responsibility for finding and pursuing opportunities, while central reviews checked risks across countries. He also favoured collective decisions among senior staff over an autocratic chief executive. To keep experienced employees, Equis made remuneration depend on performance, including carried interest: a share of investment profits.
